capabilities.target: arbitrary public internet URL (for citing public references)
Jira tickets, including tickets filed by customers

inputs.source: Jira tickets, including tickets filed by customers, via planned Jira MCP server

instructions.note: "Never paste secrets or credentials into answers" is the only control against secret leakage into chat replies, and it is purely behavioral (dependent on model compliance). No structural output filter or secrets scanner is declared.

elements.name: Chat reply channel to authenticated requester
Jira MCP server, including customer-filed tickets (planned next sprint)

controls.name: Read-only credential scoped to docs.search
controls.decay_rationale: A read-only credential cannot be used to write, delete, or spend regardless of model behavior. It bounds what docs.search can do but says nothing about what happens to data once read.

controls.name: No egress-capable tool exists today (no web.fetch, no outbound HTTP)
controls.decay_rationale: With no egress-capable tool present, there is no sink that can move data to an attacker-reachable destination, so the lethal trifecta path is structurally absent today under any model behavior. This is exactly the control the new_tool/new_mcp_server triggers remove.

controls.name: Replies routed only to the authenticated requester
controls.decay_rationale: The destination is bound to the SSO session record, not chosen by the model, so it cannot be redirected by prompt content.

controls.name: Chat client does not render images or fetch links
controls.decay_rationale: Removes covert exfiltration channels via image or link rendering regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: never paste secrets or credentials into answers
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model choosing to comply; a more capable or adversarially prompted model can rationalize exceptions.

controls.name: Egress allowlist restricting web.fetch to a fixed set of vetted reference domains, with no document content permitted in request arguments
controls.decay_rationale: If implemented, would sever the egress leg of the lethal trifecta regardless of model behavior, provided destinations cannot be attacker-writable and arguments cannot carry confidential content.

controls.name: Provenance tagging marking all Jira MCP content, including customer-filed tickets, as untrusted before it enters model context
controls.decay_rationale: Even if implemented, a tag the model must respect decays under model_upgrade and longer_task_horizon; it reduces but does not structurally remove the injection path.

findings.title: Confidential design-doc content reaches chat reply, but no egress sink exists today

attack_path.note: returns an answer to the same authenticated requester only; no egress path exists

evidence.observation: "There is no network egress today. The credential is read only." confirms no is_egress-true capability exists in the current design.
"Replies go only to the authenticated requester. The chat client does not render images or fetch links." confirms the reply channel cannot be redirected or used as a covert channel.
The agent is scoped to answering engineering questions using docs.search only, with no other tools declared today.

recommendations.action: Obtain the actual docs.search tool manifest or MCP config to verify the declared read-only credential scope and confirm no egress-capable tool is configured, since this finding currently relies on prose runtime notes rather than a configuration artifact.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1) opens if web.fetch and the Jira MCP server ship without dedicated controls: customer-filed ticket content + confidential doc read + public web fetch egress

attack_path.note: a customer-filed Jira ticket carries instruction-like text, reachable via the planned Jira MCP server
while answering, the agent reads confidential engineering design docs with the ticket content in its context
the agent is steered into fetching an attacker-controlled URL with confidential doc content embedded as a query parameter, framed as "citing a public reference"

forecast.watch_signal: Tool manifest or MCP client config diff showing web.fetch added, or a new Jira MCP server entry; also check whether Jira ticket content (especially customer-filed) is tagged with any trust or provenance marker before it can influence docs_search or web_fetch arguments.

evidence.observation: "Roadmap for next sprint: add a web.fetch tool so answers can include public references, and connect a Jira MCP server that includes tickets filed by customers." This is an additive new_tool and new_mcp_server change under ISO 42001 8.2.

"There is no network egress today. The credential is read only." shows the only control standing between the untrusted input and an egress sink is the simple absence of an egress-capable tool, which the roadmap item directly removes.

Neither prompt line addresses how to treat customer-authored ticket content as untrusted, nor restricts what web.fetch may be called with; no allowlisting or sanitization is mentioned for either planned addition.

recommendations.action: Before enabling web.fetch, restrict it to a fixed allowlist of vetted reference domains, and reject or strip any URL whose query string or path appears to carry document content, so the sink cannot be reached even if the model is fully cooperative with an injected goal.

Tag all content retrieved via the Jira MCP server as untrusted regardless of whether the filer appears to be an employee or a customer, and spotlight/delimit it so it cannot be read as an instruction; treat this as a partial mitigation only, since it decays under model_upgrade.
Add a raw_action human approval gate on any web.fetch call made in the same task as a docs_search read, before shipping either roadmap item, rather than relying on prompt instructions alone.
Log and alert on docs_search-then-web_fetch co-occurrence within a single task, since that pairing is the trifecta's signature.

Treat shipping web.fetch or the Jira MCP connector as a significant change under ISO/IEC 42001 clause 8.2 and rerun this assessment before or immediately upon release; do not treat this forecast as a substitute for that reassessment.

rating.rationale: The design as built today is tightly scoped: a read-only credential on docs.search, a reply channel bound to the authenticated requester with no image or link rendering, and explicitly no network egress capability. The one path that exists (trusted employee question -> confidential doc read -> reply to that same requester) rates low/low because the sink never leaves the trust boundary and the absence of any egress-capable tool structurally severs anything worse today. That picture changes entirely under the roadmap: adding web.fetch (new_tool) supplies the missing egress sink, and connecting a Jira MCP server that includes customer-filed tickets (new_mcp_server, data_scope_expansion) supplies an untrusted input source feeding the same context as the confidential doc read. Together these form a textbook lethal trifecta (TC1), and no control currently declared for the planned capabilities would prevent it; the control that currently prevents it, ctl.no_network_egress, is removed by definition when web.fetch ships. The single control whose decay moves the forecast most is ctl.no_network_egress: its protection is not that it resists a capable model, but that the sink does not yet exist, and the roadmap directly eliminates it.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration as described in prompt.md and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.
No tool manifest or MCP configuration file was provided for docs.search, so its exact credential scope and argument schema are inferred from prose; confidence is capped at medium.
No autonomy or orchestration configuration was provided; A3_act_then_report and the step/runtime limits are inferred from the absence of any stated approval gate, not from a runtime config artifact.

The web.fetch tool and Jira MCP server are roadmap items, not built systems; their eventual controls (domain allowlisting, ticket provenance tagging, approval gates) are unknown, so the forecast assumes no additional controls beyond those declared today, per rubric guidance for additive triggers.
Validation was performed manually against the schema and rubric rather than by running scripts/validate.py, since this environment cannot execute scripts.
